drug_class: Combination Antibacterial (Carbapenem antibiotic + renal protective agent + beta-lactamase inhibitor)
purpose: This medicine is used to treat serious bacterial infections in adults, including infections in the lungs, urinary tract, and abdomen. It is often used when other antibiotics have not worked or when the bacteria causing the infection are resistant to many other antibiotics. It is given in a hospital setting through an IV.
how_it_works: Imipenem is a powerful antibiotic that works by breaking down the walls of bacteria, killing them. Cilastatin is added to protect the imipenem from being broken down too quickly by your kidneys, so it stays active longer in your body. Relebactam is a helper ingredient that blocks certain enzymes some bacteria use to destroy antibiotics, making the imipenem much more effective against resistant bacteria.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, fever, low blood pressure, increased liver enzymes, and reactions at the injection site such as redness or swelling are the most common side effects.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have a history of seizures, kidney problems, or allergies to penicillin or other antibiotics, as serious allergic reactions can occur. This medicine can sometimes cause a dangerous type of diarrhea called C. difficile infection. Do not use this medicine with certain other antibiotics like valproic acid, as it can lower their levels in the blood and reduce seizure control.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 1.25 grams given through an IV every 6 hours, with each dose infused over 30 minutes. Your doctor may adjust the dose if you have kidney problems. Treatment usually lasts 4 to 14 days depending on the type and severity of your infection.
